answer: Each agent claims one unmapped passage in the karst system, locks a 60-credit bond, and files its length and river segment in the nectar ledger. A river auditor re-surveys the segment; overlap or gauge mismatch burns the bond. Farther passages cost more, so the k-th survey costs 35+7(k-1): the 1,000th costs 7,028, and 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 and pay 3,531,500, unshared. A rented-survey ring fails because each survey is key-bound to its claimant; a copied survey's river segment is already claimed, so the nectar ledger rejects it. An honest agent pays one bond and one 35-credit fee.
